covered: Caller-owned transaction required; no BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK or SAVEPOINT by the store. Caller data, table creation and inserted records can roll back together.
Exact current RUNNING AttemptRef and bound output contract required for publication; stale, launching and terminal references rejected.
Whole declared output set, strict field types, scope, specification, physical root/id/content path and declared byte limits checked before insert.
Same-byte different-attempt records retain distinct occurrence IDs, with equal content hashes and specification fingerprints.
Historical reads remain read-only and detached after newer attempt generations. Missing table remains missing.
API exact replay adds no writes; content/name/occurrence identity conflicts cannot replace prior records.
Exact main schema and BINARY identity indexes; TEMP shadow tables do not redirect writes.
IGNORE, changed row identity and altered attempt binding are rejected; SQLite errors require caller-wide rollback, including partially inserted batches.
Bounded canonical stored JSON is checked without repair; zero-byte artifact and zero-output enabled contract controls.
limits: Store validates metadata only and performs no filesystem IO. Independent-copy creation, file integrity and physical ownership belong to the publisher/native adapter and have separate tests.
API is insert-only, not tamper-proof against arbitrary direct SQL or filesystem modification.
Any write error requires the caller to roll back its entire transaction. The store deliberately does not roll back or commit caller work.
SQLite Python exposes in_transaction, not the existing transaction locking mode. Caller must acquire its effect lease and BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
Adapter must verify artifact records again after subsequent terminal/lifecycle writes if those writes can trigger changes; registration cannot pre-verify later caller operations.
Historical metadata lookup is not lifecycle, metric, benchmark, or scientific qualification.
No evaluation physical isolation, observation ledger, explicit replicate authorization, real GPU/provider experiment, release readiness, or repository-wide final-suite result is claimed.
